newsitem.title: UK: EMI denies report of Q3 slowdown.
newsitem.headline: EMI denies report of Q3 slowdown.

text.p: British entertainment group EMI Plc on Wednesday denied a report in the Financial Times that said fewer platinum, gold and silver record sales awards were given in the third quarter, and said quarterly figures were anyway a poor guide to sales trends.
A spokesman said that although silver awards had fallen, figures showed awards for higher-selling albums had risen.

Fewer overall awards were given out, the spokesman pointed out, but only because of a drop in silver awards. He pointed out that there had been an increase in gold, platinum, double platinum, triple platinum and multi-platinum album awards.
"Fewer albums got awards, but those fewer albums sold more copies," the spokesman said.
He declined further comment on third-quarter trading but said there were always short-term fluctuations in sales depending on the timing of releases by major artists.
The spokesman said year-on-year sales were a better guide, or fourth quarter comparisons because of the importance of Christmas sales.
Earlier EMI shares dropped as the FT report renewed fears of a slowdown in music sales. The stock closed down 17-1/2p at 12.77-1/2.
